note: North Dakota's reporting line is not staffed around the clock: live agents answer between 8am and 5pm Central on weekdays, and outside that you can only leave a message. If a child is in immediate danger at a weekend, call law enforcement rather than waiting on a callback. North Dakota law does require institutional abuse reports to be made and received the same way as every other report, so a program is not a special case.

civil_injury.summary: Two years for assault, battery or false imprisonment. Six years for negligence and other personal injury that is not an intentional tort.
civil_injury.citation: N.D. Cent. Code 28-01-18(1) (assault, battery, false imprisonment: 2 years); 28-01-16(5) (other injury to the person: 6 years)
civil_injury.quote: the following actions must be commenced within two years after the claim for relief has accrued: 1. An action for libel, slander, assault, battery, or false imprisonment.
civil_injury.note: 28-01-16(5): 'An action for criminal conversation or for any other injury to the person or rights of another not arising upon contract, when not otherwise expressly provided' must be commenced within six years. Sexual-assault claims have their own rules (28-01-25.1, 28-01-25.2), not covered here.

civil_minor_tolling.summary: Partly. Time while you are under 18 does not count, but the extension can last no longer than one year after you turn 18. In practice the deadline is your 19th birthday or the normal deadline counted from the injury, whichever is later. No general extended deadline for physical (non-sexual) child abuse.
civil_minor_tolling.quote: the time of such disability is not a part of the time limited for the commencement of the action. However, the period ... cannot be extended more than five years by any such disability except infancy, nor can it be extended in any case longer than one year after the disability ceases.
civil_minor_tolling.note: The one-year-after-18 cap is unusual and harsh: a child hurt at 12 in an assault has until 19, not 20. For a six-year negligence claim, if six years from the injury runs past 19 that later date should govern because the extension only lengthens, never shortens, the period. Confirm reading with a lawyer.

civil_government_claims.summary: For claims against the State of North Dakota, written notice must go to the Office of Management and Budget within 180 days after the injury is discovered (one year for a serious injury), and the suit must be filed within three years; claims against cities, counties and other political subdivisions must be filed within three years.
civil_government_claims.citation: N.D. Cent. Code 32-12.2-04(1) (notice), 28-01-22.1 (state, 3 years), 32-12.1-10 (political subdivisions, 3 years)
civil_government_claims.quote: A person bringing a claim against the state or a state employee for an injury shall present to the director of the office of management and budget within one hundred eighty days after the alleged injury is discovered or reasonably should have been discovered a written notice
civil_government_claims.note: 28-01-22.1 (in https://www.ndlegis.gov/cencode/t28c01.pdf): 'an action against the state or its employees ... must be commenced within three years after the claim for relief has accrued', accruing on discovery. 32-12.1-10 (https://www.ndlegis.gov/cencode/t32c12-1.pdf): political-subdivision actions 'must be commenced within three years'. No notice requirement found in chapter 32-12.1. The notice period excludes time the person was incapacitated by the injury.

criminal_child_abuse.summary: Three years from the offense for felony child abuse. There is no pause until the child turns 18 for physical abuse; the child-victim extensions apply only to sexual offenses and trafficking.
criminal_child_abuse.quote: Except as otherwise provided by law, a prosecution for any felony other than murder must be commenced within three years after its commission.
criminal_child_abuse.note: 14-09-22 (abuse of child) is a class C felony, class B if the child is under six, and class B when committed by a paid caregiver 'who provides care, supervision, education, or guidance for a child unaccompanied by the child's parent' - relevant to residential programs. 29-04-03.1 and 29-04-03.2 (longer periods, clock starting at 15) cover only chapter 12.1-20 sexual offenses and trafficking. 29-04-04 stops the clock while the defendant is out of state.

criminal_felony_assault.summary: Three years from the offense for aggravated assault and other felonies. Misdemeanor (simple) assault: two years.
criminal_felony_assault.quote: A prosecution of a misdemeanor or infraction, except as otherwise provided by law, must be commenced within two years after its commission.
criminal_felony_assault.note: Aggravated assault under 12.1-17-02 is a class C felony (3 years under 29-04-02). Time the defendant spends outside North Dakota is not counted (29-04-04).

channels.name: North Dakota Board of Counselor Examiners
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines professional counselors in North Dakota.
channels.how: The complaint process begins once the Board's formal complaint form is signed and returned to its office.

channels.name: North Dakota State Board of Psychologist Examiners
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines psychologists, registrants and psychology residents in North Dakota.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist, registrant or psychology resident.
channels.how: Complete and sign the Board's complaint form, setting out the nature of the allegation and the facts behind it. You may attach supporting documents.

channels.name: North Dakota Board of Social Work Examiners
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses social workers in North Dakota and ensures they comply with the laws and regulations governing the practice.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It cannot take a complaint over the phone, and the form has to be signed.
channels.how: Send a written, signed complaint to the Board.

channels.name: North Dakota Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Line
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide report line. North Dakota law requires reports of known or suspected institutional child abuse or neglect to be made and received in the same way as any other report.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a North Dakota program.
channels.how: Call. Live agents answer 8am to 5pm Central on weekdays; outside those hours you can leave a message. If a child is in immediate danger, contact law enforcement.
channels.phone_note: Live 8am to 5pm Central, Monday to Friday. Messages can be left outside those hours.

channels.name: North Dakota HHS licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses North Dakota's child care and residential facilities and investigates complaints that one has breached the licensing standards.
channels.how: Contact Health and Human Services. Abuse and neglect go to the reporting line.
channels.phone_note: Child and Family Services; toll free 1-800-245-3736.

channels.name: North Dakota Protection and Advocacy Project
channels.what_it_can_do: North Dakota's federally mandated P&A, with authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A North Dakota program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
